Oregano
Closely related to marjoram, oregano has
a woody stalk with small green leaves.
Considered less sweet than marjoram, it is
thought to have a stronger, more peppery
flavor.  A ubiquitous pizza sauce flavoring,
oregano is also widely used in Mediterranean
cuisine (mainly Italian and Greek) and in
meat and poultry dishes.  Oregano retains
its flavor when dried.

Allspice
Also known as Jamaican pepper, allspice is
ground from the hard brown berries of the
allspice tree, which grows in Mexico and
throughout the Caribbean.  Allspice is so
named because it imparts the flavor of
nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon.  An excel-
lent addition to marinades, allspice is also
used to flavor cured and jerked meat,
desserts, and sauces.  It is also an ingredient
